speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have a history of chronic cough and recurrent bronchitis; to determine the underlying cause, we need to clarify your symptoms. How long has this cough been persisting, and does it worsen at night or with specific activities?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old woman. The patient has been experiencing an aggressive cough producing copious amounts of thick, foamy, yellow-green sputum for about 11 years, with exacerbations similar to the current presentation today. Reports that the cough is worse in the morning and has had multiple evaluations in the past due to recurrent bouts of bronchitis requiring antibiotics treatment. The patient is a non-smoker.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Bronchiectasis

The 11-year duration, "aggressive" cough with copious thick, foamy, yellow-green sputum, and morning predominance despite a non-smoking history are classic for bronchiectasis. I will need to see a Chest CT to confirm the diagnosis and rule out other causes.
